terms.definition: A diagram showing an element's symbol surrounded by dots for its valence electrons.
terms.function: Predicts how many bonds an atom can form at a glance.
terms.whereItIs: The three dot diagrams in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the everyday shorthand chemists use to picture bonding.

terms.definition: One dot drawn per valence electron around an element's symbol.
terms.function: Shows how many electrons the atom has available for bonding.
terms.whereItIs: The teal dots on the three tiles in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: The dots are the entire message of a Lewis structure.

terms.definition: A pair of dots shared between two symbols, representing a covalent bond.
terms.function: Shows two atoms sharing valence electrons to hold together.
terms.whereItIs: The dot pairs that become the rods of the methane molecule.
terms.whyItMatters: Shared pairs are how a Lewis structure draws a real bond.

terms.definition: Using an atom's dot count to predict how it will bond.
terms.function: Tells you the number of bonds an atom can form before any reaction.
terms.whereItIs: Carbon's four dots predicting four bonds to hydrogen.
terms.whyItMatters: Prediction is the whole point of drawing Lewis structures.
